s: Four Roman villas, mosaic floors that earned UNESCO status
w: Still under excavation, this coastal park holds the bulk of ancient Nea Paphos: four Roman villas - the Houses of Dionysos, Aion, Theseus and Orpheus - with elaborate mosaics. An agora, a Hellenistic-Roman theatre and the Tombs of the Kings necropolis lie within its grounds, part of the 1980 UNESCO listing.
_facts: Archaeological park in Kato Paphos containing the main part of ancient Greek and Roman Nea Paphos
Four major Roman villas with well-preserved mosaics: Houses of Dionysos, Aion, Theseus and Orpheus
Also contains an agora, asklepieion, basilica, odeion, Hellenistic-Roman theatre and the Tombs of the Kings necropolis
Part of the Paphos complex inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1980

s: Rebuilt after an earthquake flattened its predecessor
w: This fortress guarding the western end of Paphos harbour dates to the mid-13th century, built after a 1222 earthquake destroyed its predecessor, Saranta Kolones, some 600 metres to the northeast. The replacement has held its post at the water's edge ever since.
_facts: Fortress at the western end of Paphos harbour, dating to the mid-13th century
Built to replace Saranta Kolones, an earlier fortress destroyed by the 1222 earthquake

s: A ruined basilica dedicated to 'Our Lady of the Harbour'
w: Built at the start of the 5th century and dedicated to 'Our Lady of the Harbour,' this basilica once stood a short walk from Paphos harbour, now ruined within the Archaeological Park. Colourful mosaics and a handful of restored columns still survive among the harbourside restaurants nearby.
_facts: Ruined basilica built early 5th century, dedicated to Panagia Limeniotissa ('Our Lady of the Harbour')
Located within the Paphos Archaeological Park, north of Paphos harbour
Surviving mosaics and restored columns visible on site

s: A Byzantine church inside the UNESCO-listed old quarter
w: This Byzantine Church of Cyprus church sits at the centre of Kato Paphos, within the very district that UNESCO inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1980 for its mosaics and ancient remains. A working church still, it stands amid a quarter otherwise given over to Roman ruins.
_facts: Byzantine Church of Cyprus church at the centre of Kato Paphos
Part of the area inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1980

s: Five rooms of finds, Neolithic to 1700 AD
w: Five rooms trace Cyprus from the Neolithic era to 1700 AD, built mostly from finds unearthed at Palaepaphos (Kouklia), Nea Paphos and Marion-Arsinoe (Polis). Among the holdings: skeletal remains recovered from 31 tombs near Nea Paphos's eastern seafront, excavated between 1980 and 1983.
_facts: Museum in Paphos with five rooms spanning the Neolithic to 1700 AD
Artefacts mainly from Palaepaphos (Kouklia), Nea Paphos and Marion-Arsinoe (Polis), plus surrounding villages
Includes skeletal remains from 31 tombs excavated near Nea Paphos's eastern seafront, 1980-83
